title: odd-teaser must use LLM-based artifact detection
decision: odd-teaser MUST use LLM-based artifact detection (odd-scribe style) to watch user journaling and surface potential learnings/decisions for user confirmation
context: odd-teaser v1.1 was implemented as a manual categorization form requiring users to click buttons to classify their writing. User explicitly stated they would delete such a system. The implementation completely missed the product intent.
rationale: User explicitly stated manual categorization is unacceptable
odd-scribe already demonstrates the correct pattern (detect scents, user confirms)
ODD principle: use-only-what-hurts means the system should reduce friction not add it
consequences: odd-teaser must be reimplemented with LLM detection
System watches journaling for learning/decision/override scents
User confirms surfaced artifacts rather than manually categorizing

evidence.ref: user_quote: If I had to click buttons and decide myself what I just wrote was wholesale categorized as learning, decision, or override, I'd delete the system
